findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions.lean:792 `theorem nhds_pi ... := by simp only [nhds_iInf, nhds_induced, Filter.pi]`; :807 `tendsto_pi_nhds ... := by rw [nhds_pi, Filter.tendsto_pi]`.
findings.fix: Replace the clause with an accurate one, e.g. "`ι` need not be finite: convergence in the product topology is componentwise, so this is Mathlib's `tendsto_pi_nhds`."
findings.issue: Docstring claims "the two sides are the same statement about the same filter". They are equivalent, not identical: `tendsto_pi_nhds` rests on `nhds_pi`, a proved lemma, not `rfl`. The file elsewhere marks genuine defeq explicitly (`isRestricted_iff`: "which is `Iff.rfl`"), so this reads as a false defeq claim — and it is proof commentary rather than a description of the result.

findings.evidence: Lines 58-60 list `isRestricted_monomial`, `isRestricted_of_hasFiniteSupport`, `IsRestricted.smul`, `restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubmodule`, `mem_restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubmodule`; the diff touches lines 34-35 (Main definitions) but no Provenance line.
findings.fix: Add both names to the "**Original here.**" list.
findings.issue: The module docstring's Provenance section enumerates every declaration by attribution group ("Three groups, because the port and this PR did different things to different declarations"), but `isRestricted_pi_iff` and `mem_restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubmodule_pi_iff` are added to "Main definitions" only. A reader consulting Provenance cannot tell whether they derive from AINTLIB.

summary: The new declarations are documented and the not-simp rationale on the submodule lemma checks out, but `isRestricted_pi_iff`'s docstring misstates the equivalence as definitional and the Provenance section was not updated for either new declaration.
